name_note: The GTDB genus Bilophila matches the genus of the same name in the literature; the work cited here concerns its species Bilophila wadsworthia.

sentences.text: Bilophila wadsworthia is a Gram-negative anaerobic rod that is strongly catalase-positive, is stimulated by bile, and does not reduce sulphate.
It was isolated from intra-abdominal specimens of patients with gangrenous and perforated appendicitis, and subsequently also from normal faecal specimens.
A study reported that in germ-free mice fed a high-fat diet, colonisation relied on microcompartment and anaerobic energy-metabolism genes that metabolise taurine and isethionate.
That study describes Bilophila wadsworthia as a sulfidogenic bacterium linked to inflammation and gut barrier dysfunction, whose expansion is promoted by high-fat diets.
In two population-based cohorts, higher Bilophila abundance was reported to be associated with reduced basal ganglia volumes and with elevated liver enzymes and triglycerides.
